title: Setup → Sharing Rules lists only stored rules once declared rules leave sys_sharing_rule (objectstack C3 stage 9)
body:
Filing gate **④**: a coordination node, the objectui half of objectstack-ai/objectstack C3 stage 9 (objectstack-ai/objectstack#23952, PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#24376), filed by the objectstack epic seat (`epic:#15194`, `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3`) as its cross-repo follow-up. ⛔ Not a claim. Reader who acts: the epic seat dispatches it once stage 9 has merged. Dedupe: semantic search on objectstack-ai/objectui, "Setup sharing rules list declared rules package rules not shown registry" → 0 hits.

Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#24421

<sub>Re-pointed by the epic seat when objectstack-ai/objectstack#23952 closed (PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#24376 merged `5e979073`): stage 9's half is done. Re-pointed again at 2026-10-19T01:35Z when C9's PR #12998 merged (`78b07f4`): that file-surface serialization is cleared, and #7611 stays open only for its objectstack-side remainder. This card now waits on objectstack-ai/objectstack#24421, the server's guard and reconcile under ruling B′ (below). Setup's New and Edit on a sharing rule exercise both, and building the page before they land would mean building it twice.</sub>

## Ruling B′ on objectstack-ai/objectstack#24378 (6257388265) changes this card's shape

Ruling B′ binds 「`sharing_rule` is charted under regime O, guarded」. Its items 1, 2 and 4, verbatim:
> 1. … a stored `sys_sharing_rule` row of the declared rule's name, in its scope, replaces the declared rule whole; `active: false` on that row is the switch-off …
> 2. **The guard.** Creating a `sys_sharing_rule` row, or renaming one, to the name of a declared rule in that scope through Setup's New (or any write that is not an edit of the projected declared row) is refused at the write door with the vendor rule named. Editing the projected row — the customised copy — stays the way to narrow or switch off a vendor rule, as today.
> 4. **Under a wall** an organisation's overlay is its own …; under `single` the one overlay answers everywhere (today's behaviour).

So the original **Wanted** and **Acceptance** below, which say declared rules render "read-only", are superseded on that point:
- A declared rule is listed with its provenance and is editable. Its Edit writes the customised copy: a stored row of the same name in the caller's scope, which is how a vendor rule is narrowed or switched off.
- A customised declared rule shows once, as customised, with no second row beside it. An organization-authored rule stays editable as before.
- New does not offer a declared rule's name. If the server refuses one (objectstack-ai/objectstack#24421's guard), the page shows that refusal, which names the vendor rule.

The one-list rule and 「**There is no merged two-source list.**」 still bind. The dev measures which existing server read answers "declared, customised, or organization-authored" for each row. If none does, that gap belongs to the server and gets reported there; the client does not merge two sources to fill it.

## What changes on the objectstack side

Stage 9 retires `bootstrapDeclaredSharingRules`. A sharing rule a package declares is read from the registry at enforcement, and the ownership ceremony deletes the `sys_sharing_rule` rows that mirrored it. A fresh boot writes zero `sys_sharing_rule` rows for declared rules. Organization-authored rules stay rows.

The objectstack dev and the contract reviewer both measured the consequence (os-dev-report on objectstack-ai/objectstack#23952, `out_of_scope_findings`; record 6253094552 on PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#24376):
- Setup's Sharing Rules page is the generic `sys_sharing_rule` object view. Once the PR lands, it lists organization-authored rules only, and a package's declared rules disappear from Setup while they still grant access.
- `GET /api/v1/sharing/rules` (the sharing service) lists both declared and stored rules.
- Reach: every deployment whose packages declare sharing rules (showcase 2; the maintainer's hotcrm 11).

## Wanted

Setup shows the declared rules again, without a client-side merge of two sources. objectui#7611's rule binds here too: 「**There is no merged two-source list.**」. The two shapes that rule leaves:
- **A.** The Sharing Rules page reads one server list, `GET /api/v1/sharing/rules`, which already answers both kinds. Declared rules render read-only with a provenance badge; stored rules stay editable. Search, sort and paging are the server's.
- **B.** Declared rules get their own read-only catalog page from `/api/v1/meta/sharing_rule`, as C9 built for positions and permission sets. The data page stays the `sys_sharing_rule` view for organization rules.

Measure first which shape the existing console code supports with the least new surface, and say why in the PR. The pick has to keep native search, sort and paging.

## Acceptance

- On a showcase boot that carries stage 9 and objectstack-ai/objectstack#24421, Setup lists the showcase's two declared sharing rules with their provenance, and any organization-authored rule. A declared rule's Edit writes the customised copy; switching it off sets `active: false` on that copy. New with a declared rule's name shows the server's refusal.
- No request fetches and merges two lists in the client.
- objectstack's `.objectui-sha` pin moves after this lands; the objectstack epic seat dispatches that.
